hotContext.criticalNews: Post-Q2: AI5 volume production still guided to 2027 ('hopefully next year'); Samsung/TSMC credited for Optimus compute investment and Micron for multi-year memory allocation. AI6 remains aspirational ('best edge chip') with no new tape-out date. Training compute (Cortex 1/2) >200 MW combined in Texas. No public AI5 wafer/yield/board metrics.

recentKeyChanges.title: Q2 Call: AI5 Volume Still 'Hopefully 2027'; Samsung/TSMC/Micron Named; AI6 Boast Unbacked
recentKeyChanges.description: On Tesla's July 22, 2026 Q2 earnings call, Musk reaffirmed that AI5 is expected in volume production 'hopefully next year' (2027), saying the chip design team 'exceeded expectations' — a design-quality compliment, not a production pull-forward. He publicly thanked Samsung and TSMC for major compute-capacity investments supporting Optimus (and robotaxi) silicon, and thanked Micron for a 'significant' multi-year memory allocation at 'reasonable' terms amid what he called 'pretty insane' memory prices (a 'hundred-year flood' / biggest price jump he has seen). Nikkei and TrendForce quote Musk claiming AI6 will be 'the best edge computing chip in the world' while development continues; no AI6 tape-out or production date was advanced beyond prior mid-2028 framing. Official Q2 shareholder deck quantifies Cortex training clusters (Cortex 1 >90 MW, Cortex 2 >115 MW in production; onsite Texas MW more than doubled in H1 2026) but contains no AI5 wafer starts, yield figures, or board-volume milestones. Reality check: Samsung foundry-side AI5 tape-out (July 13) already filed last week; volume AI5 remains H2 2027 / vehicle meaningful deployment 2028+; Cybercab and current fleets still ship on AI4; memory allocation is necessary insurance in a shortage, not proof of inference-chip ramp.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Named foundry/memory partners and 'design exceeded expectations' sound bullish, but AI5 volume date is unchanged at 2027, AI6 claim is unbacked marketing, and no new wafer/yield/board metrics were disclosed.

Samsung and TSMC explicitly credited for major compute investments tied to Optimus/robotaxi silicon scale-up

Cortex 1 >90 MW and Cortex 2 >115 MW both in production; Tesla onsite Texas training compute (MW) more than doubled in H1 2026 (Q2 shareholder update)
Dual-source AI5 path (Samsung Taylor 2nm + TSMC) still intact after July 13 foundry tape-out context
negative_signals: AI5 volume still 2027 — no acceleration vs prior mid/late-2027 guidance; nearly ~2 years behind original timelines
No disclosed AI5 wafer starts, yield %, engineering-sample qualification status, or completed board counts toward the 'hundreds of thousands of boards' line-switchover bar
AI6 'best edge chip in the world' is aspirational PR with no new tape-out/date; AI6 previously slipped toward mid-2028 on Samsung 2nm risk
Vehicles, Robotaxi Model Ys, and Cybercab still launching/shipping on AI4 (or AI4.x) — AI5 not in commercial hardware yet
Memory 'win' is defensive amid industry-wide DRAM shortage (Cook/Musk 'hundred-year flood'); does not prove inference-chip manufacturing readiness
Q2 deck's only AI Inference Compute paragraph focuses on early-stage Austin semiconductor fab (Terafab path) — foundry partners still carry near-term volume risk
Not a Tesla App / call summary: vehicle production also described as electronics/chip constrained alongside batteries — supply tightness, not abundance

recentKeyChanges.title: Micron Multi-Year Memory Allocation Highlighted; AI Board BOM Still Supply-Risk Bound
recentKeyChanges.description: Coverage of the July 22 earnings call (TrendForce 2026-07-23, Wccftech 2026-07-22, Bloomberg headline) centers on Musk thanking Micron for making 'room for Tesla in the years to come' with significant memory allocation at non-panic pricing. TrendForce frames this against Micron's Strategic Customer Agreements (3–5 year price+volume locks; 16 SCAs covering ~20% DRAM / ~1/3 NAND at Micron's prior call) and notes auto OEMs already face multi-billion DRAM inflation. For Tesla AI computers, high unified memory (Electronics Weekly's July 13 A15/AI5 writeup cited up to 144GB-class configs in secondary coverage — treat as unverified spec chatter) makes DRAM a first-class BOM risk alongside Samsung/TSMC logic wafers. Positive for de-risking Optimus/Robotaxi board builds if allocation is real; critical caveat: allocation ≠ free capacity, terms are undisclosed, and logic foundry 2nm yield at Taylor remains the gating item for AI5 volume — memory thanks do not move the AI5 production clock.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Multiple outlets quote Musk on Micron allocation, but contract size/price/duration are undisclosed and memory relief does not resolve 2nm AI5 manufacturing risk.

positive_signals: Musk on-call thanks to Micron for significant multi-year memory allocation at 'reasonable' prices (transcript quotes via TrendForce/Investing.com)
Public signal that Tesla secured DRAM amid industry shortage while peers (e.g., Apple/GM) warn of price shock
Aligns with Optimus scale-up narrative naming TSMC, Samsung, and Micron as key silicon partners (Digitimes/Nikkei secondary)
negative_signals: No disclosed volume, ASP, or SCA contract details — cannot verify 'significant' or 'reasonable'
Industry DRAM shortage ongoing; allocation can be re-prioritized if hyperscalers bid higher
Does not address Samsung Taylor 2nm yield or AI5 wafer start schedule — still the primary production gate
AI5 board volume for vehicles still not expected until 2027+; memory reservation is pre-positioning, not shipment evidence

key_metrics.actual: Qualitative Micron allocation only; no public unit or $ figure
key_metrics.target: Secure DRAM/HBM-class supply for AI5/AI6 boards and Optimus at scale
key_metrics.trajectory: Supply-chain de-risking messaging; manufacturing proof still missing
